text:
maya: Quick heads-up — the sample-app embedding flow is failing in the wild when using the JS SDK. curl to /v1/embeddings works but the SDK call returns a 400.

maya: curl that works:
`curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{ "model": "rdb-embed-1", "input": "hello" }'`

maya: SDK call (what sample-app currently uses):
`await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'rdb-embed-1', input: 'hello' })`

maya: Error from SDK: `400 Bad Request: Unknown parameter: model` — looks like the SDK is expecting `engine` instead of `model`.

sam: Yup, we had an internal param rename on the REST side (model -> model) but historically our older SDKs used `engine`. New REST accepts `model`, but the published JS client on npm still validates `engine`.

sam: TL;DR: param drift between REST and SDK. We shipped docs update but didn't publish a client patch.

juan: I opened a PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/342) that adds backward-compat mapping (accept `model` and map to `engine`). Tests green but I didn't publish the new npm package yet.

devex-bot: CI passed on main for js-sdk PR #342 — ready for release. Task created: devex/release#78 (assign to sam).

leila: Two suggestions: 1) patch sample-app to detect `model` and transparently call `client.embeddings.create({ engine: model, ... })` as a hotfix, 2) add a deprecation warning when `engine` is used so users migrate cleanly.

emily: One more wrinkle — some folks are hitting 401s because sample-app env var name is `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but the SDK checks `RW_API_KEY`. So it's a small onboarding friction too. Log snippet: `Error: 401 Unauthorized (no Authorization header)`.

maya: Ugh yes I hit that locally. The quick fix: update README + code to check both env names and emit a helpful message.

raj: Let's not forget retries — the SDK's default retry/backoff for embeddings is different from REST client libs in other languages. If we publish a patch, include a changelog entry: "parameter aliasing for embeddings + consistent auth env names + retry policy harmonization".

maya: I'll push a tiny PR to sample-app now with fallback mapping + env checks. Patch snippet I'll include: 
```js
const key = process.env.RW_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
if (!key) console.warn('Missing API key. Set RW_API_KEY or REDWOOD_API_KEY.');
const params = userParams.model ? { engine: userParams.model, input: userParams.input } : userParams;
await client.embeddings.create(params);
```

sam: Perfect. After Maya's patch lands, I'll cut the npm release for js-sdk and tag a minor. Please add a note to the release that samples may need the env var fix. :shipit:

juan: I'll follow up and publish the npm package once the release ticket is assigned.

maya: Thanks all — filing a follow-up issue to add an automated integration test between the sample apps and the latest published SDK so this doesn't regress. Issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/example-apps/issues/112

leila: Nice. If anyone runs into other parity gaps (auth header names, retry semantics, streaming differences), drop them here and we can triage.

emily: FYI I pushed a tiny README note to the sample-app repo with the env var workaround.

maya: Closing loop — sample-app PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/example-apps/pull/211 (includes mapping + env check). Last message here for thread.
